occupation.note: 'Daniel Elston & [illegible]', soap and candle manufactory, paying cash for tallow and house ashes - Chicago Democrat, 26 November 1833. The word after the ampersand is obliterated by an ink blot on the scan and 'Co.' is a reasonable expansion rather than a reading.

persons.note: A MANUFACTURER, WHICH THE 1835 TOWN HAS ALMOST NONE OF. Buying tallow and house ashes is buying the by-products of the packing trade and of every household fire in the town, which makes this one business a measure of how many households there were. Andreas has a Daniel Elston running the largest of the city's five brickyards by 1854 - two decades past the scene and evidence of nothing about 1835 except that the man stayed. The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 is the only contemporary Chicago document this project holds; an advertiser in it was paying to be found, which makes it strong evidence of existence and address in November 1833 and weak evidence of survival to 1 July 1835, nineteen months and about 2,400 people later. THE FEDERAL TRACT SALES — A TRANSACTION, NOT A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales database records this name entering federal ground around the town: “ELSTON DANIEL” — 1 sale on 1836-06-18, T39N R14E sec 08 (ls0047). A sale is a TRANSACTION and never a residence — the register's Residence column reads 'UNKNOWN' here, so it says a man of this name was buying land in these years and nothing about where he lived or what stood on the ground. The reading is transcription-mediated; the adjudication is data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the grade is applied by T-0515 against every source at once, and a purchase corroborates rather than mints.

research_note: THE ONLY CHEMICAL WORKS IN THE 1835 DATASET, and the household that best shows what a single advertisement can imply about a population. A soap and candle manufactory buying tallow implies slaughtering (this dataset models three packing and slaughter buildings) and buying house ashes implies wood fires in a lot of houses, which is the population K1 is trying to count.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.

address_later.note: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 prints this address against this person, in the entry quoted on the card: 'Elston, Daniel, patent press-brick maker, res North Branch [died September 13, 1855, aged 65]'. It is evidence about 1843, written here as 1843's and read back onto no 1835 claim. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. The value is the volume's own line, split by its crosswalk on the entry's punctuation. These volumes set the trade first and its qualifiers after it on the same line, so the split may carry an employer, a market or a corner along with the trade. The printed entry is quoted beside the value for exactly that reason: the split is checkable against it, and neither is read into an 1835 claim.

back_projection.note: NOT READ BACK, BECAUSE SOMETHING BETTER ALREADY STANDS. Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 prints an address against this name in 1843, and it is left where it is. An 1835 placement already stands: this household works at `elston_soap_candle_manufactory`, and clause 2 says an attested 1835 placement always beats a door printed 8 years later. The later address stays on the record as 1843's evidence and moves nothing.
